title: Lamb Tagine with Apricots and Almonds
subtitle: Moroccan slow-cooked lamb with dried apricots, spices, and almonds
excerpt: Tender lamb shoulder slow-cooked with Moroccan spices, dried apricots, and honey until the sauce is thick and fragrant. Scatter with toasted almonds and fresh coriander.

recipe.sourceNotes: A tagine is both a Moroccan cooking vessel (a conical earthenware pot) and the slow-cooked stew made in it. Moroccan cuisine is characterised by its combination of sweet and savoury elements and the use of warm, fragrant spices such as cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and ginger rather than chilli. The sweet-savoury combination of meat cooked with dried fruit is a feature of both Moroccan and Persian cooking, derived from medieval Arab culinary traditions in which fruit was used to add acidity and sweetness to meat. A tagine can be cooked in a conventional casserole with a lid; a real tagine vessel is not required. Serve with couscous or flatbreads.

recipeTools.notes: A large casserole with a lid.

content.text: Lamb shoulder is the correct cut for a tagine: it has enough fat and connective tissue to break down during the long, slow braise without drying out. Leg will become dry. Add the dried apricots and honey in the last 30 minutes of cooking so they soften but do not dissolve entirely. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden before scattering over; raw almonds have much less flavour.
Heat the oil in a large casserole over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches until golden. Remove and set aside. Reduce to medium.

Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, and all the spices. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. Return the lamb. Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer.

Cover and cook over a very low heat (or in the oven at 160 C / fan 140 C) for 1 hour 30 minutes. Add the dried apricots and honey and cook for a further 30 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the sauce is thick. Taste for seasoning. Scatter with toasted almonds and coriander. Serve with couscous or flatbreads.
